1.title: Job sanctified his children
1.text: After their feasts, Job offered burnt offerings for each child, fearing: 'It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts.'

1.question: What did Job offer for his children after their feasts?
options: Burnt offerings
Peace offerings
Grain offerings
Silent prayers

1.question: What did Satan insinuate about Job's fear of God?
options: That Job feared God for nothing, only out of self-interest
That Job's righteousness was only outward, hiding wickedness in his heart
That Job only obeyed God out of fear of punishment
That Job's sons had secretly cursed God in their hearts without his knowledge

1.question: Who fell upon the oxen and donkeys and slew the servants?
options: The Sabeans
The Chaldeans
Job's sons
Job's friends

1.question: How did Job react to losing everything?
options: 'The Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord'
'He tore his clothes, cursed God aloud, and drove away all his servants in anger'
'He accused his servants of stealing his flock and drove them all away in fury'
'He fled into the desert and hid himself away in shame and sorrow'

2.question: What did Satan ask the Lord in the second test?
options: To touch Job's bone and his flesh
That He send fire from heaven upon Job's house
That He take the life of Job's remaining faithful servants
That He afflict his mind with nightmares

2.question: What did Job's wife say to him?
options: 'Curse God, and die'
'Be patient and wait'
'Flee to another land'
'Call your friends'

2.title: Seven days in silence
2.text: The three friends sat with Job on the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word, for they saw that his grief was very great.

2.question: How long did the friends sit with Job without a word?
options: Seven days and seven nights
Forty days and forty nights
Twelve full days and nights
Three full days together

3.question: What did Job curse at the start of this chapter?
options: The day he was born
The name of the Lord
His wife
His friends

3.title: Why did I not die at birth?
3.text: Job asks why he did not die from the womb, for then he 'should have lain still and been quiet,' at rest from his affliction.

3.question: What does Job say he would do had he died at birth?
options: He would lie still and be at rest
He would reign over every nation of the earth
He would return stronger to fight once more
He would soon see the face of God

3.question: To what does Job compare the rest he longed for?
options: A hidden untimely birth that never sees the light
A king who reigns forever in great glory and honor
A mighty warrior who conquers every battle he faces
A hired servant well paid for his labor

3.question: Who does Job say rejoice and are glad?
options: Those who find the grave
The mighty kings of all the earth
The rich who are full of silver and gold
The strong and valiant young men

3.question: How does Job describe his state at the chapter's end?
options: He was never at rest, but trouble came upon him
He regained all the peace and joy he had before the trial
He felt great comfort and relief throughout his whole soul
He no longer felt any pain or sorrow at all

4.question: What is Eliphaz's argument about the innocent?
options: That no innocent person ever perished
That all the righteous suffer equally
That God punishes even the upright without cause
That suffering comes without any cause

4.title: The image of the lion
4.text: Eliphaz uses the lion as a figure: the roaring and the teeth of the lions are broken, and the old lion perishes for lack of prey — so ends the wicked.

4.question: What figure does Eliphaz use for the wicked's end?
options: The lion whose teeth are broken
The eagle that soars to the clouds
The river that overflows and destroys all
The tree full of good fruit

4.question: What came upon Eliphaz in the night vision?
options: Fear and trembling, which made his bones shake
A great deep joy that filled his heart with peace
A soft voice that greatly praised him before everyone
A truly wonderful dream full of riches

4.question: According to the vision, how do those in houses of clay die?
options: They die without wisdom
They die in great honor
They live forever
They are spared by God

5.question: What does Eliphaz say happens to the foolish man's children?
options: They are far from safety and crushed in the gate
They receive great wealth and live in full peace and security
They are exalted to high places and receive honor from the wise
They become wise and prosper in the land

5.title: Marvels without number
5.text: Eliphaz declares that God 'doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number'.

5.question: How does Eliphaz describe God's works?
options: Great and marvellous without number
Mighty and filled with great splendor
Simple and repeated every single year
Few and without much importance

5.question: How does God treat the wise, according to Eliphaz?
options: He takes them in their own craftiness
He honors them before all people with abundance
He forgets them completely and abandons them
He gives them a long and peaceful life

5.question: What paradox does Eliphaz state about God's hands?
options: He woundeth, and his hands make whole
He exalts the humble and humbles the proud
He keeps silent before all human suffering
He judges but never truly forgives

5.question: With what shall the one God restores be in league?
options: With the stones of the field
With the armies of the neighboring kings
With the wild beasts of the desert
With the angels of heaven

5.question: How does Eliphaz close his counsel to Job?
options: He says it is so and bids Job to know it for his good
He promises great riches to whoever faithfully follows his counsel
He threatens to abandon Job forever if he does not keep silent before God
He says Job is guilty and deserves punishment

6.question: What comparison does Job make to justify his crying out?
options: Even the wild donkey does not bray over fresh grass
The strong lion roars when it feels great hunger while hunting
The royal eagle flies high when it seeks its own prey
The ox rests calmly beside the green pasture

6.question: What consolation does Job say he would yet have?
options: That he has not concealed the words of the Holy One
Recovering all his lost possessions from his early youth
Seeing all his enemies finally punished by God himself
Returning to his youth and former strength

6.title: The duty of a friend
6.text: Job affirms that to the afflicted, a friend should show pity, even to one who has forsaken the fear of the Almighty.

6.question: What does Job say a friend owes the afflicted?
options: Pity
Silence
Riches
Punishment

6.question: To what does Job compare his treacherous friends?
options: To brooks that dry up and vanish
To firm mountains that never move
To perennial springs that never dry
To trees full of good fruit

6.question: What does Job deny having asked of his friends?
options: To deliver him from the oppressor or redeem him
To give him silver and gold taken from their treasures
To remain silent and speak no further word at all
To leave and abandon him in his affliction

6.question: What question does Job ask about his tongue?
options: Whether there is iniquity in his tongue
Whether he should remain silent before his friends
Whether he lied to his own faithful friends
Whether he deceived his friends with lies

7.question: How does Job describe his flesh in this chapter?
options: Clothed with worms and clods of dust
Strong as bronze and full of great vigor
Whole and renewed as in the days of youth
Covered with glory and splendor

7.title: The cloud that vanishes
7.text: Job says that, like the cloud that is consumed and vanishes, he who goes down to the grave shall return no more to his house.

7.question: To what does Job compare one who goes down to the grave?
options: The cloud that vanishes and returns not
The firm mountain that never once trembles
The perennial river that never stops flowing
The fixed star in the firmament

7.question: In his anguish, what would Job's soul choose?
options: Strangling and death rather than life
The return of prosperity and all his goods
The sincere forgiveness of all his faithful friends
A long life full of peace and rest

7.question: What does Job ask of God at the chapter's end?
options: To pardon his transgression before he lies in the dust
To increase his punishment even more until he cannot bear it
To destroy forever all his friends and his own household
To give him great riches and many strong sons

8.question: What condition does Bildad set for God to restore Job?
options: That Job be pure and upright
That Job pay his friends
That Job leave the land of Uz
That Job renounce his children

8.title: The papyrus without mire
8.text: Bildad asks whether the rush grows without mire or the flag without water — a figure that, without God, the hypocrite's hope withers.

8.question: What figure does Bildad use for the hypocrite's hope?
options: The rush that withers without mire
The palm tree that withstands storms
The wheat that ripens without rain
The vine planted on the rock

8.question: To what does Bildad compare the wicked who seems prosperous?
options: To a green plant that is rooted out of its place
To an evergreen tree that never dries out nor withers away
To an everflowing spring that never once runs dry
To a firm rock that never moves nor falls

8.question: What does Bildad say will happen to the dwelling of the wicked?
options: It shall come to nought
It shall be exalted
It shall last forever
It shall be rich and safe

9.question: What work of God does Job describe at the start?
options: He removes the mountains, and they know not
He rains down fire upon the cities of the wicked
He parts the great sea in two before the people
He rains down manna from heaven for the people

9.question: What constellations does Job say God made?
options: Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades
Taurus, Scorpio, and the Southern Cross
The Serpent, the Lion, and the Three Marys
The Southern Cross and the moon

9.title: How to answer God?
9.text: Job asks: if even the proud helpers stoop, 'how much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?'

9.question: Why does Job doubt he could answer God?
options: Because even the proud helpers stoop before Him
Because even the warrior angels tremble before him
Because no wise man ever dares to contest his words
Because he greatly fears the wrath of the Almighty

9.question: When force is spoken of, what does Job say of God?
options: Lo, he is strong
That he is weak
That he is like men
That he can be summoned

9.question: What complaint does Job make about the earth?
options: It is given into the hand of the wicked
It is entirely covered by the darkness of sin
It is subject to the judgment of angels
It is utterly lost beyond all remedy

9.question: Feeling condemned, what does Job ask?
options: Why he should labor in vain
Why he lost the blessing of God
Why the heavens grew silent
Why he was utterly forsaken

9.question: What does Job say is lacking between him and God?
options: A daysman who might lay his hand upon them both
An angel who might intercede for his cause before God
A priest who might offer atonement on his behalf
A king who might defend him in judgment

10.question: Why does Job ask if God has eyes of flesh?
options: To question whether God sees as man sees, searching his sin
To assert that God always sees everything with perfect clarity
To recall that the eyes of the Lord never grow weary of watching
To ask that God would turn away His wrath from him

10.title: Formed like clay
10.text: Job reminds God: 'Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews' — he asks the Creator to remember whom He formed.

10.question: With what does Job remind God He clothed him?
options: Skin and flesh, bones and sinews
With scales and feathers, claws and beak
With wool and hide, horns and hooves
With roots and green leaves

10.question: To what does Job compare how God hunts him?
options: As a fierce lion
As a meek sheep
As a dove
As a lamb

10.question: How does Job describe the land to which he will go?
options: A land of darkness and the shadow of death, without order
A land of dense darkness where no one can ever find the way
A wholly dry and barren land where nothing can flourish
A land of utter silence and eternal, bitter cold

11.question: What harsh charge does Zophar make against Job?
options: That God exacts of him less than his iniquity deserves
That Job hides secret sins which God already knows well
That Job always speaks with greater wisdom than the elders
That Job deserves to be praised among the wise of the earth

11.title: God knows vain men
11.text: Zophar affirms that God 'knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also' — nothing escapes Him, even what seems hidden.

11.question: What does Zophar say God knows and sees?
options: Vain men and wickedness
Pure hearts and sincere faith
Just prayers and holy sacrifices
The secrets of the distant future

11.question: What does Zophar promise Job if he purifies himself?
options: He shall forget his misery as waters that pass away
That he shall receive riches greater than he had before he suffered
That his friends shall publicly admit that he was right all along
That God shall reveal to him the exact reason for all his suffering

11.question: How does Zophar say the hope of the wicked ends?
options: It shall be as the giving up of the ghost
It shall be crowned with everlasting honor
It shall be safely kept until the final day
It shall be remembered for generations

12.question: How does Job describe the contempt of those at ease?
options: They despise the one ready to slip, like a lamp held in scorn
They mock the aged and despise the wisdom that long life brings
They are ashamed before the mighty and hide their own fear from all
They mock the just and the upright without any reason at all

12.title: All life in God's hand
12.text: Job declares that in God's hand 'is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.'

12.question: What does Job say is in God's hand?
options: The soul of every living thing
Only the fate of the kings of the earth
The strength and wisdom of the wise counselors
The power of the princes

12.question: What power over the waters does Job attribute to God?
options: He withholds the waters and they dry up; he sends them and they overturn the earth
He makes the earth quake and causes the mountains to crumble into countless pieces
He gathers the clouds together and pours down fire upon the wicked and rebellious cities
He divides the mighty sea and dries up every river of the entire land

12.question: What does God do to the trusted and the aged, per Job?
options: He removes the speech of the trusty and the understanding of the aged
Gives the trusty ones power over many kingdoms and nations of the earth
Grants the aged everlasting glory and abundant riches forevermore and always
Multiplies the days and honor of the wise and aged elders

12.question: How do the chiefs whose heart God takes away wander?
options: They grope in the dark, staggering like a drunken man
They march victorious over the neighboring nations with great might
They reign with justice and wisdom over all the peoples of the earth
They rest peacefully within their own homes

13.question: What ironic counsel does Job give his friends?
options: That they hold their peace, for it would be their wisdom
That they confess all their sins before the whole assembly
That they pray without ceasing until God gives them a clear answer
That they depart at once and leave him in total peace

13.title: Speaking for God with deceit
13.text: Job warns his friends: God will reprove them if they secretly accept persons and speak wickedly on His behalf.

13.question: Of what does Job warn friends who speak for God?
options: That God will reprove their partiality
That they will be rewarded with honor before all the people
That they will grow wise and understanding forever before God
That they will reign with power over the nations

13.question: What declaration of trust does Job make here?
options: 'Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him'
'I will curse the day I was born and wish I had never lived'
'I will never open my mouth to speak of these things again'
'My friends speak nothing but the plain truth about me'

13.question: What two things does Job ask of God before he speaks?
options: To withdraw His hand, and not let His dread terrify him
To restore his lost possessions and renew his former health
To destroy forever all those who mock at his affliction
To give him new children to replace the ones he lost

13.question: To what does Job compare the man who wastes away?
options: To rottenness and a garment eaten by the moth
To a firm rock that never shakes despite the wind
To a fruitful tree planted beside the flowing waters
To a mighty river that never runs dry

14.question: What question does Job ask about clean and unclean?
options: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one
Who will make the unclean a king over all the nations of the earth?
Who purifies the heavens and makes the stars shine forever?
Who measures the sea and counts every one of its waves?

14.question: What contrast does Job draw between the tree and man?
options: A felled tree sprouts again, but where is man when he dies?
Both live forever and never come to know death or any decline at all
Man sprouts again like the tree, but the felled tree never returns
Neither one of them ever perishes nor turns to dust at all

14.title: The steps numbered
14.text: Job says to God: 'now thou numberest my steps,' feeling that his every move is watched because of his sin.

14.question: What does Job feel God does with his steps?
options: Numbers them and watches his sin
Blesses them every day with abundance and joy
Forgets them completely and never thinks of them again
Multiplies them for no reason at all

14.question: How does Job describe the state of the man who passes?
options: His flesh has pain and his soul mourns within him
He is in full joy and sings praises without ceasing
He is exalted among kings and receives great honors
He feels nothing at all, for he already rests in peace

15.question: Of what does Eliphaz accuse Job's mouth?
options: Of uttering his iniquity and choosing the tongue of the crafty
Of speaking words of wisdom and righteousness before God and all the people
Of speaking with humility and fear before the Almighty and His justice
Of teaching righteousness and comfort to those who suffer unjustly

15.question: What authority does Eliphaz invoke against Job?
options: Among them are gray-haired men, older than Job's father
Among them are prophets who spoke with angels of the Lord
Among them are wise kings who ruled over many ancient nations
There is an angel who revealed to him the secrets of heaven

15.title: Not even the heavens are pure
15.text: Eliphaz affirms that God 'putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight' — how much less man.

15.question: What does Eliphaz say about the heavens in God's sight?
options: They are not clean
They are perfect
They are unworthy
They are forgotten

15.question: How does Eliphaz describe the life of the wicked?
options: Tormented all his days
Surrounded by riches and constant honor
Protected by peace and eternal prosperity
Filled with constant blessings

15.question: Why, according to Eliphaz, does the wicked suffer?
options: Because he stretches out his hand against God and defies Him
Because he despises the poor and mistreats the needy of the land
Because he abandons faith and seeks the wisdom of the wicked
Because he denies the existence of the Almighty God

15.question: What will happen to the branches of the wicked?
options: The flame shall dry them up
They shall be green forever
They shall bear much fruit
They shall be watered by God

15.question: What, according to Eliphaz, do the hypocrites conceive?
options: Mischief, and bring forth vanity
Goodness, and bring forth fruits of righteousness
Wisdom, and teach uprightness to the sons of men
Peace, and bring comfort to the afflicted

16.question: How does Job say he would treat his friends if they were in his place?
options: He would strengthen them with his mouth and assuage their grief
He would accuse them of lies and mock their affliction openly and harshly
He would abandon them to their own fate without any true comfort at all
He would punish them with very harsh and bitter words

16.question: How does Job describe the attack of those gathered against him?
options: They gaped with their mouth and smote him on the cheek in scorn
They brought him rich gifts and honored him before everyone present
They prayed for him and begged God for mercy with many bitter tears
They gave him true comfort and words of hope and peace

16.title: Sackcloth and dust
16.text: Job tells that he sewed sackcloth upon his skin and defiled his head in the dust — deep signs of his mourning and humiliation.

16.question: What signs of mourning does Job describe?
options: Sackcloth on his skin and his head in dust
A crown and royal robe upon the shoulders of a king
Feasting and songs of joy throughout the whole city
Gold and silver scattered along the road

16.question: What does Job say about the path he will soon take?
options: He shall go the way whence he shall not return
He will return to prosperity and live many years in peace
He will overcome his friends and be exalted among the people
He will reign among men with great honor

17.question: What saying does Job utter about one who flatters friends?
options: The eyes of his children shall fail
He shall be crowned with honor before all the people
He shall live in peace and prosperity all his days
He shall prosper forever with great abundance

17.title: No wise man among them
17.text: Job challenges his friends to return, but declares 'I cannot find one wise man among you' — he has lost hope of comfort from them.

17.question: What does Job conclude about his friends?
options: He finds no wise man among them
They are the wisest men who ever lived on earth
They are wholly right and deserve full trust
They are faithful and worthy of trust

17.question: Where does Job say his hope shall descend?
options: To the bars of the pit, to rest in the dust
To the throne of kings, to reign in eternal glory
To the heavens of light, to dwell among the angels
To fertile fields, to rest in peace

18.question: What does Bildad say happens to the light of the wicked?
options: It shall be put out, and his spark shall not shine
It shall shine forever and never grow dim nor fade away
It shall light the righteous and grow brighter every day
It shall grow each day with great intensity

18.title: Hidden snares
18.text: Bildad describes a cord laid in the ground and a trap in the way — figures of how the wicked falls into his own ruin.

18.question: What figures does Bildad use for the wicked's ruin?
options: A hidden cord and a trap
A throne and crown lost forever
A spring and garden fenced with thorns
A shield and sword broken

18.question: What shall be scattered upon the wicked's dwelling?
options: Brimstone
Gold
Flowers
Dew

18.question: How does Bildad sum up the place of the wicked?
options: It is the place of him that knoweth not God
It is the house of the righteous who fear the Lord
It is the throne of kings who govern with wisdom
It is the garden of the blessed in heaven

19.question: What does Job say of his error, if indeed he has erred?
options: His error remaineth with himself
God himself will bear the guilt for it
His children will inherit the guilt of it
It will be forgotten in time

19.question: How does Job say God has counted him?
options: As one of His enemies
As a dear friend
As a son
As a faithful servant

19.title: A stranger in his own house
19.text: Job relates that his breath became strange to his wife and even his servant gave no answer — he is forsaken by all his own.

19.question: To whom did Job's breath become strange?
options: To his own wife
To his enemies
To kings
To strangers

19.question: Why does Job beg his friends for pity?
options: Because the hand of God has touched him
Because he wanted to prove his innocence to the king
Because his friends had stolen his inheritance
Because he feared imminent death

19.question: What is Job's great declaration of faith in this chapter?
options: 'I know that my redeemer liveth'
'God has forgotten me forever in this suffering'
'There is no justice at all under the sun'
'My friends speak the pure truth'

19.question: What warning does Job give his friends at the end?
options: That they fear the sword, for there is a judgment
That they depart from the king's presence forever
That they confess before all their guilt against him
That they offer sacrifices for their sins

20.question: How long, according to Zophar, does the joy of the wicked last?
options: It is brief, but for a moment
It lasts as long as the life of the righteous
It remains firm forever and never ends
It grows as time passes by

20.title: Restoring to the poor
20.text: Zophar says the children of the wicked shall seek to please the poor, and his own hands shall restore the goods he took.

20.question: What will the wicked's hands do, per Zophar?
options: Restore the goods he took
Build temples for the priests
Distribute gold among the poor of the city
Raise altars to the Lord

20.question: What will God do with the riches the wicked swallowed?
options: He shall cast them out of his belly
He shall keep them for his children
He shall turn them into eternal blessings
He shall divide them among the poor

20.question: What peace does Zophar say the wicked does not feel?
options: He felt no quietness in his belly
He knew no rest among his friends
He found no comfort in his riches
He had no peace with his children

20.question: What image of judgment does Zophar use for the wicked?
options: The drawn sword comes out of his body, with terrors
An army of angels descends upon his tent to destroy it
Fire from heaven consumes his entire house and all his goods
A great storm tears his tents into the wind

20.question: How does Zophar sum up the lot of the wicked man?
options: It is the portion God appoints him as a heritage
It is the reward reserved for those who fear the Lord
It is the blessing promised to the children of the promise
It is the common fate shared by all mankind

21.question: What gesture does Job ask of his friends in their astonishment?
options: To lay their hand upon their mouth
To tear their garments in sign of mourning
To fall prostrate with their face to the ground
To be silent and listen closely

21.question: What does Job observe about the cattle of the wicked?
options: Their bull breeds without fail and their cow does not cast her calf
It miscarries all its young before they are ever born into the world
It is devoured by wild beasts roaming across the wide open field
It sickens and dies shortly after it is finally born

21.question: What question do the wicked ask about the Almighty?
options: 'What is the Almighty, that we should serve him?'
'What profit would it give us to follow him all our days?'
'What sign would he give us to prove his mighty power?'
'When will he come to judge all the earth in justice?'

21.question: What does Job ask about the wicked once he is dead?
options: What pleasure has he in his house when his months are cut off?
Who will care for his children and goods after he departs this life?
Who will inherit his throne and all his accumulated riches?
Who will remember him after his house has fallen?

21.question: What contrast does Job draw between two men who die?
options: One dies in fullness and another in bitterness, yet both lie in the dust
One dies covered in honors, and another dies forgotten by all his children
One dies surrounded by riches, and another dies begging forgiveness from his enemies
One dies filled with great joy, and another dies in deep despair

21.question: What does Job say happens to the wicked in the day of destruction?
options: He is reserved and brought forth in the day of wrath
He is destroyed at once without any mercy shown
He is exalted among the kings and princes of the earth
He is forgotten by God forever and ever

21.question: How does Job characterize his friends' consolations?
options: Vanity, for in their answers remains falsehood
True wisdom, for it comes directly from God
Words of God, full of justice and truth
Perfect counsel, without any flaw at all

22.question: Of what does Eliphaz accuse Job regarding his brothers?
options: Of taking pledges without cause and stripping the naked
Of denying them bread and water in famine and thirst
Of seizing their fields and driving them from their lands
Of falsely accusing them before the elders

22.question: Why does Eliphaz say Job is surrounded by snares?
options: Because of his supposed wickedness
Because he is very righteous before God
Because he loves the poor more than himself
Because he fears God with all his heart

22.title: The way of the wicked
22.text: Eliphaz warns that Job walks 'the old way which wicked men have trodden,' who were cut down out of time, their foundation overflown with a flood.

22.question: What way does Eliphaz say Job walks?
options: The old way of wicked men
The path of the righteous who fear God
The road of kings and mighty rulers
The broad way that leads to life

22.question: What counsel does Eliphaz give Job so good may come to him?
options: To acquaint himself with God and be at peace
To accuse his friends before all the people
To hide his sins from everyone around him
To flee the land and seek refuge elsewhere

22.question: What does Eliphaz promise Job if he turns back?
options: He shall delight in the Almighty and lift up his face to God
He shall conquer mighty kingdoms and be feared by all nations
He shall live a thousand years surrounded by great riches
He shall defeat his friends in judgment before everyone

22.question: How, per Eliphaz, will even one not innocent be delivered?
options: By the pureness of Job's hands
By his own strength and courage
By riches gathered throughout his life
By luck and good fortune alone

23.question: What would Job do if he found God's court?
options: He would lay out his cause and fill his mouth with arguments
He would flee in fear before the presence of the Almighty
He would stay silent, saying nothing at all before him
He would accuse his friends of speaking against him

23.question: How does Job say he will come forth after God tries him?
options: As gold
As dross
As dust
As ashes

23.title: Not silenced by darkness
23.text: Despite his dread of God, Job affirms he was not cut off by the darkness, nor did the gloom cover his face.

23.question: What does Job affirm about the darkness around him?
options: He was not cut off by it
It was dispelled by God before its time
It made him invisible to the eyes of men
It made him fall silent before everyone

24.question: To what does Job compare those who go forth early to their prey?
options: To wild donkeys in the desert
To lions that roar at night in the forest
To eagles that soar high over the mountains
To wolves that hunt in packs

24.question: What injustice does Job denounce against the poor?
options: They make the naked go without clothing and take the sheaves from the hungry
They give them abundant bread and shelter, protecting them well from the cold night
They clothe the needy with the finest garments and pay them generous wages every day
